The *Hatthiṅgapañha* ("The Elephant", Mil 7.5.10) is a section of the *Milindapañha* [SuttaCentral]. Belonging to the work's exposition on similes and spiritual qualities, the text considers the commendable attributes (*aṅga*) of an elephant as spiritual models [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records three modern translations in three languages [SuttaCentral].

SuttaCentral notes that material associated with or mentioned in the text connects to a wide array of canonical and post-canonical literature, including verse traditions such as the Pali *Dhammapada* (Dhp 361), the Gāndhārī *Dharmapada* (G-Dhp 51–90), the Patna *Dharmapada* (P-Dhp 50–64), and the Sanskrit and Tibetan *Udānavarga* recensions (UV 7, UVS 7, Uv Kg 7), as well as Chinese translations (T 210.34, T 212.8, T 213.7) [SuttaCentral].
